places.name: Assam
places.summary: Rhinos at Kaziranga, the river island of Majuli, Ahom monuments at Sivasagar, the Kamakhya Temple — and half of India's tea.
places.seoTitle: Assam Travel Guide: Kaziranga, Majuli & Guwahati
places.seoDescription: Plan Assam: Guwahati and Kamakhya, Kaziranga's rhinos, Majuli's satras, Sivasagar's Ahom monuments, Manas, getting there and when to go.

overview.text:
Assam grows nearly half of India's tea. Kaziranga, a UNESCO site, shelters two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinos; Manas, on the Bhutan border, is another UNESCO park.

Guwahati, with the Kamakhya Temple, is the gateway; up the Brahmaputra lie Majuli, the world's largest inland river island and the home of the satras, and Sivasagar, the old Ahom capital.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Guwahati's Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi airport, about 28 km from the city, is the main airport of the Northeast — the busiest in the region and India's 10th busiest, with flights from across the country.

By rail: Guwahati in the west and Dibrugarh in the east are the state's two well-connected hubs.

By road: the same two cities, Guwahati and Dibrugarh, are the main road hubs.

places.name: Sikkim
places.summary: A small Himalayan state under Kanchenjunga: monasteries, high lakes, the Nathu La border pass and plastic-free green rules.
places.seoTitle: Sikkim Travel Guide: Gangtok, Pelling & North Sikkim
places.seoDescription: Plan Sikkim: Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La, Pelling and Pemayangtse, Yumthang and Gurudongmar, permits, getting there and the best time.

images.alt: Kanchenjunga rising above the hills of Sikkim
images.caption: Kanchenjunga from Pelling

overview.text:
Sikkim sits in the Eastern Himalayas beneath Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain and India's highest, and is home to the UNESCO-listed Khangchendzonga National Park. It is a green state too — plastic water bottles are banned.

Gangtok, the capital, is the base for Rumtek Monastery, Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La. West Sikkim's Pelling has close views of the Kanchenjunga range and the Pemayangtse Monastery; North Sikkim rises to the Yumthang Valley and Gurudongmar Lake, one of the highest lakes in the world.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Bagdogra airport near Siliguri is the gateway to Gangtok. Sikkim's Pakyong airport has no operating flights at present.

By rail: the nearest major stations are Siliguri Junction and New Jalpaiguri in West Bengal.

By road: NH 10 runs from Siliguri to Gangtok, about 124 km — some five hours by road.
